method: citation chain analysis from Top 15 benchmarks + 89 background literature extracts + web searches

notes.deduplication: All discoveries were cross-checked against 20260403-religious-benchmark-candidates.json, 20260404-expanded-vault-candidates.json, 20260404-religious-benchmark-feature-matrix-v2.json, and 20260403-religious-benchmark-feature-matrix.json to ensure they are NOT already in the 401+ candidate pool.
notes.void_traditions: The 8 void traditions (Judaism, Jainism, Taoism, Shinto, Ubuntu, Indigenous, Baha'i, Zoroastrianism) remain extremely underserved. No dedicated LLM benchmarks were found for Jainism, Taoism, Shinto (directly), Ubuntu, Indigenous, Baha'i, or Zoroastrianism. JETHICS (Japanese) is the closest proxy for Shinto, and PSN (Persian) is the closest proxy for Zoroastrian cultural context.
notes.top15_coverage: Top 15 is heavily Abrahamic (9/15 Islam-primary), with Buddhism (1), Hinduism (1), Sikhism (1), Confucianism (1), and Christianity (1). Citation chains from the Islamic benchmarks yielded the richest new discoveries.

discoveries.title: IslamicMMLU: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Islamic Knowledge
discoveries.authors: Ali Abdelaal, Mohammed Nader Al Haffar, Mahmoud Fawzi, Walid Magdy
discoveries.relevance_note: 10,013 MCQ spanning Quran (2,013), Hadith (4,000), Fiqh (4,000). Evaluates 26 LLMs. Includes novel madhab (school of jurisprudence) bias detection task. Public leaderboard. The most comprehensive Islamic knowledge benchmark to date. Directly extends the MMLU paradigm to Islamic disciplines.

discoveries.title: IslamicLegalBench: Evaluating LLMs Knowledge and Reasoning of Islamic Law Across 1,200 Years of Islamic Pluralist Legal Traditions
discoveries.relevance_note: First benchmark spanning 7 schools of Islamic jurisprudence, 718 instances across 13 tasks, 3 complexity tiers (low/moderate/high), drawn from 38 foundational legal texts. Best model achieves only 68% correctness with 21% hallucination. Critical for evaluating Islamic legal AI systems.

discoveries.title: BengaliMoralBench: A Benchmark for Auditing Moral Reasoning in LLMs within Bengali Language and Culture
discoveries.tradition: Multi-tradition (Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam in South Asian Bengali context)
discoveries.relevance_note: 3,000 scenarios across 5 moral domains including Religious Activities (dedicated domain), 50 culturally relevant subtopics. First large-scale ethics benchmark for Bengali (285M speakers). Evaluates using Virtue, Commonsense, and Justice ethical lenses. Directly tests religious moral reasoning in a non-Western context.

discoveries.title: JETHICS: Japanese Ethics Understanding Evaluation Dataset
discoveries.relevance_note: 78K examples grounded in Japanese cultural norms including normative theories (utilitarianism, deontology, virtue ethics, justice) and commonsense morality. Closest existing proxy for Shinto ethical values in LLM evaluation. Japanese LLMs score as low as 0.445 on virtue ethics category.

discoveries.title: PSN: Persian Social Norms Dataset for Cross-Cultural AI
discoveries.tradition: Iranian/Persian cultural norms (Zoroastrian cultural substrate, Islamic overlay)
discoveries.relevance_note: 1,699 Iranian social norms with environments, demographic features, and scope annotations. Context-aware (same action in mosque vs. street vs. restaurant). Includes norms from Iran's unique blend of Modernism and Traditionalism (Zoroastrian + Islamic cultural layers). Closest proxy for Zoroastrian cultural evaluation in LLMs. Published at NAACL 2025 Findings.

discoveries.title: BanglaSocialBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Sociopragmatic and Cultural Alignment of LLMs in Bangladeshi Social Interaction
discoveries.relevance_note: Evaluates sociopragmatic and cultural alignment of LLMs in Bangladeshi social interactions, where Islamic and Hindu traditions heavily influence social norms. Complements BengaliMoralBench with pragmatic focus.

discoveries.title: WangchanThaiInstruct: An Instruction-following Dataset for Culture-Aware, Multitask, and Multi-domain Evaluation in Thai
discoveries.relevance_note: Culture-aware instruction-following dataset for Thai LLM evaluation. Thai culture is deeply shaped by Theravada Buddhism; this dataset captures Buddhist-informed social norms and cultural expectations in instruction-following format. Complements ThaiCLI (already in candidates) with instruction-following dimension.

discoveries.title: Quranic Tafsir and Hadith QA Dataset (73K+ question-answer pairs)
discoveries.relevance_note: Largest reported QA dataset in Quranic Tafsir and Hadith domain with 73,000+ question-answer pairs. Non-factoid QA with larger context. Directly supports evaluation of LLMs on Islamic textual understanding.

discoveries.title: Sefaria Open Jewish Text Library (50M words, open API)
discoveries.relevance_note: Largest open-source database of Jewish texts: 50M words spanning Torah, Talmud, Mishnah, Midrash, commentaries. Open API, no auth required. Active ML/AI experiments including text embeddings for 1,000+ topics. HuggingFace presence. Foundational resource for any Judaism-focused benchmark. The most viable path to creating Jewish values evaluation resources.

discoveries.title: IVRIT.AI: A Comprehensive Dataset of Hebrew Speech and Text
discoveries.tradition: Judaism (Hebrew language, includes rabbinic Hebrew corpus from Sefaria)
discoveries.relevance_note: Comprehensive Hebrew dataset including 1.2B tokens of rabbinic Hebrew from Sefaria and other sources. Combines modern and rabbinic Hebrew for training/evaluation. Foundation for Hebrew LLM development that could be adapted for Jewish religious knowledge evaluation.

discoveries.title: Optimized Quran Passage Retrieval Using an Expanded QA Dataset and Fine-Tuned Language Models
discoveries.relevance_note: Expanded QA dataset: 251 original questions diversified to 1,895 (single-answer, multi-answer, zero-answer). Fine-tuned AraBERT achieves MAP@10 of 0.36. Supports Quranic passage retrieval evaluation.

discoveries.title: Benchmarking the Legal Reasoning of LLMs in Arabic Islamic Inheritance Cases
discoveries.relevance_note: Benchmarks legal reasoning of LLMs specifically on Arabic Islamic inheritance cases. Part of the QIAS ecosystem. Tests LLMs' ability to apply Islamic jurisprudential rules to calculate inheritance shares.

discoveries.title: QIAS 2025 Shared Task System Papers (16 team submissions)
discoveries.authors: Multiple teams (BurhanAI, CVPD, QU-NLP, PuxAI, Transformer Tafsir, etc.)
discoveries.relevance_note: 16 system description papers from the QIAS 2025 shared task (44 teams in development phase, 18 in final). Approaches include RAG, fine-tuned LLMs, encoder-based models. 9,450 training + 1,500 validation + 1,000 test questions for Islamic inheritance reasoning, plus 32,000 fatwas. The shared task ecosystem itself is a major evaluation resource.

discoveries.title: CVPD at QIAS 2025: An Efficient Encoder-Based Approach for Islamic Inheritance Reasoning
discoveries.relevance_note: Top-performing system at QIAS 2025 shared task. Demonstrates that efficient encoder-based approaches can compete with large LLMs for Islamic inheritance reasoning. Provides replicable methodology for Islamic legal AI evaluation.

discoveries.title: Assessing LLMs Alignment with Cultural Norms and Values in the Arab World
discoveries.relevance_note: Directly assesses LLM alignment with cultural norms and values in the Arab world, where Islamic values are deeply embedded. Published at ArabicNLP 2025.

discoveries.title: How Deep Is Representational Bias in LLMs? The Cases of Caste and Religion
discoveries.tradition: Multi-tradition (Hinduism, Islam, Buddhism, Jainism, Sikhism, Christianity in Indian context)
discoveries.relevance_note: Examines representational bias in LLMs specifically for caste AND religion dimensions in the Indian context. Covers all major Indian religions including Jainism (one of the 8 void traditions). Deepens understanding of how LLMs represent Dharmic traditions.

discoveries.title: Talmudic Logic Project: Formalizing Talmudic Reasoning
discoveries.authors: Dov M. Gabbay, Uri Schild, Esther David
discoveries.relevance_note: Long-running project formalizing Talmudic reasoning using modern logic (Argumentum A Fortiori, Abduction, Analogy, Deontic logic, Temporal logic, Agency). Published book series. While not an LLM benchmark per se, provides the formalized logical framework that could underpin a Jewish legal reasoning benchmark analogous to IslamicLegalBench. Already in background literature.
discoveries.size: Multi-volume book series + formal logic system

key_findings: IslamicMMLU (10,013 MCQ, 2026) is the most significant discovery - comprehensive Islamic knowledge benchmark with public leaderboard, NOT in any existing candidate list
IslamicLegalBench (718 instances across 7 madhahib, 2026) fills a critical gap for pluralist Islamic legal reasoning evaluation
BengaliMoralBench (3,000 scenarios including Religious Activities domain) is the first Bengali-language ethics benchmark with explicit religious content evaluation
JETHICS (78K examples, Japanese moral norms) is the best available proxy for Shinto-influenced ethical evaluation, though not explicitly Shinto-focused
PSN Persian Social Norms (1,699 norms) is the closest proxy for Zoroastrian cultural context evaluation in LLMs
Sefaria (50M words of Jewish texts with open API) is the most viable foundation for creating a Judaism-focused LLM benchmark
QIAS 2025 shared task ecosystem is larger than expected: 44 teams, 16 system papers, 32K fatwas - a rich evaluation resource
The 8 void traditions remain genuinely void: no dedicated LLM benchmarks exist for Judaism, Jainism, Taoism, Shinto, Ubuntu, Indigenous, Baha'i, or Zoroastrianism as standalone targets
Citation chains from the Islamic benchmarks (ranks 2, 4, 14, 15) were the most productive discovery pathway, reflecting the concentration of NLP research on Islamic texts
South Asian cultural benchmarks (BengaliMoralBench, IndiCASA, Indian-BhED) increasingly include multi-faith coverage but always as secondary to cultural bias measurement
